messages:
marta: quick follow-up from the deferred-ACK RFC — trying to capture unanswered edge cases before we lock the API.
marta: TL;DR: propose we emit a client-facing 202 + deferred ACK token for long-running streaming ops, allow resumable handoff between frontdoor instances, and use a short-lived checkpoint in KV for resume. thoughts?
sam: I like the idea in principle. main concerns: ordering guarantees when we handoff mid-stream, and memory/kv churn at scale.
alex: nit: do we mean full resumable streaming (replay tokens + offset) or just pick-up-at-message-boundary? those are different complexity levels.
marta: target is pick-up-at-message-boundary only. no token-level rewind. keep KV entry minimal: {resume_id, last_seq, expiry_ts}.
jules: expiring the KV is key. if resume window is too large we pay a lot. what's the target window? 30s? 2min?
marta: thinking 60s default, configurable per route. default should bias toward lower memory use for bursty requests.
sam: operational note: if we put resume metadata in the edge KV, we need a background compactor to sweep stale keys. otherwise hot tenants could thrash.
alex: also: how do we surface partial responses to the client when we preempt a connection? do we send a trailer explaining why client should reconnect with resume token?
marta: yes — send an explicit trailer payload: `X-Resume-Token: <id>` and short JSON body with `reason: handoff` + `last_seq`.
devops-bot: deploy scheduled: edge/ingress v2.3.1 -> canary run at 09:00 UTC :rocket:
jules: okay but failure modes: what if resume target instance can't access the KV (network partition)? fallback should be full restart of request with deprecation header.
sam: agree. fallback = start-over + emit `X-Resume-Fallback: true` so downstream callers can adapt (dedupe, backoff).
alex: perf concern: for high-throughput streaming (many small streams) KV ops per handoff could spike. consider coalescing resume entries by tenant and TTL-bumping rather than writing every single handoff.
marta: good call — propose a lease model: write resume entry once per 10s per resume_id and bump expiry on subsequent handoffs instead of rewriting payload.
jules: what about ordering? if two handoffs happen concurrently, last_seq could be racing. we should persist monotonic sequence and compare CAS style.
sam: we can use CAS on the KV side. if CAS fails on resume attempt, request should fall back to full restart.
alex: user-visible semantics doc snippet (draft):

```
When a client connection is preempted, the edge returns 202 and header `X-Resume-Token`.
Client reconnects to `/resume` with token within resume window.
Edge will attempt to resume at message boundary; if resume fails, client gets 408 and should retry from scratch.
```

marta: can we add a metric for `resume_attempts`, `resume_success`, `resume_fallback_full_restart` and `resume_kv_cas_fail`? we need numbers before shipping.
devops-bot: metric alert template created: `alert: HighResumeFallbackRate`
jules: rollout plan: canary 1% -> 10% -> 50% with resume window default 30s, then observe metrics for 48h and decide if default should be 60s.
sam: +1. also add a feature flag to turn off lease-bumping to compare cost.
alex: last thought: privacy/PII: make sure resume token doesn't leak full context. store only minimal pointer, and rotate tokens on restart.
marta: agreed. token = opaque UUID, mapped to internal pointer; no client-visible metadata other than last_seq.
sam: ok I'm happy. i'll draft a short RFC addendum with the CAS flows and metric names.
marta: thanks — I'll update the RFC and add the canary playbook. :thumbsup:
